newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar secures more LNG sales to South Korea firm.
newsitem.headline: Qatar secures more LNG sales to South Korea firm.

text.p: Korea Gas Corporation of South Korea has exercised an option to buy an additional 2.4 million tonnes of gas annually from Qatar's Ras Laffan LNG Company (Rasgas) in return for a five percent stake in the company's equity, Rasgas said on Wednesday.

"It (Rasgas) has reached agreement in principle to increase its sales of liquefied natural gas to Korea Gas Corporation (Kogas) from 2.4 million metric tonnes per annum under an existing sales and purchase agreement to 4.8 million tonnes per annum," said a company statement.
It said the sales and purchase deal was a 25-year supply agreement with first deliveries in 1999.

Korea Gas Corporation signed a deal in 1995 to buy 2.4 million tonnes a year of LNG from Rasgas from mid-1999. It also had an option under the agreement to raise the amount by another 2.4 to three million tonnes a year from 2000.

Rasgas, which is designed to eventually produce 10 million tonnes a year, is 66.5 percent owned by the state's Qatar General Petroleum Corporation (QGPC) and 26.5 percent by Mobil Corp. Japan's Nissho Iwai holds four percent and Itochu three percent.
Qatar on Monday officially opened its first LNG plant, ushering the tiny oil producer into the league of the world's major gas exporters.
Realised at the cost of $7 billion, the Qatar Liquefied Gas Company project is designed to produce six million tonnes a year of LNG - all committed to eight Japanese companies for 25 years from 1999.
Foreign energy firms are pouring billions of dollars into Qatar to develop the Gulf Arab state's massive gas reserves and increase its exports of crude oil.

Qatar, which has the world's third largest reserves of gas after Russia and Iran, has planned LNG projects to supplement its oil income -- the lowest in the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) at under $3 billion a year.
Gulf-based analysts have predicted that foreign investors will keep a close eye on Qatar as it develops its enormous gas potential.
Qatar earlier this month said it had invested $17.85 billion in the oil and gas sector in the past four years to boost production capacity and exploit gas reserves.
The country has invested heavily in a number of petrochemical and fertilisers projects in partnership with foreign companies.
